obligations.text: `under` is true only when both operands are valid segmented text on the declared separator and the ancestor's segments are a proper prefix of the value's segments, compared byte for byte; it is never true for a text prefix that ends inside a segment, and no case folding, Unicode normalization or trimming is applied.

An operand that is unresolved makes the step or condition reading `under` unresolved with that operand's reason (spec 002 3.10.4), and an operand that is empty or has an empty segment is `invalid_input`; neither is ever evaluated as false.
Every committed definition, plan, judgment, evidence and run golden keeps its bytes and `PlanId`, and a `rustev.definition/1` using `under` is refused with category 11 `requires_definition_2`.

sectionHeadings: 066: Definition predicate: segment ancestry on a declared separator (amends 002 and 032)
record.summary: A proposed amendment of approved specs 002 (3.8, 3.9) and 032 (3.1, 3.12), for release 0.5.1 (#509). A partner rule needs "this location slug sits under that city slug", for example `us:ny:new-york:soho` under `us:ny:new-york`; today the host projects the slug's parent into the snapshot and the rule compares with `member_ref`. This spec adds one predicate to the registry `rustev.exact/2`, `under{value, ancestor, separator}`, true when the ancestor's segments are a proper prefix of the value's segments on a separator the definition declares, so `us:ny:new-york-city` is not under `us:ny:new-york`. Comparison is by bytes with no normalization; an operand with an empty segment is `invalid_input`, and an unresolved operand makes the reading step unresolved, never false. Definition 1 refuses it; plans that do not use it keep their bytes and `PlanId`.
